text:
Marathon Petroleum stock has risen 13.2% over two weeks, with today's modest gain capping a sharp rally that accelerated over the past four days. The core driver is crude oil prices: U.S. oil hit $101.91 today, and Brent crude touched $110 last week, lifted by Iran's escalating attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and threats of further retaliation if the U.S. strikes again. Higher oil prices directly improve refinery margins—the spread between what refiners pay for crude and what they sell refined products for—and U.S. refineries are running at 93.5% capacity to capture that advantage.

There's a secondary layer adding to margins: tanker costs have surged, meaning the *physical cost* to deliver oil has jumped roughly $38 per barrel on top of crude prices, squeezing competitors who lack flexible supply chains while rewarding large, well-positioned refiners. The geopolitical tension remains unresolved, keeping oil volatility elevated and refinery profitability structurally higher than it was two weeks ago.
